dir="auto">BBB runs as website, so whenever a server is compromised, the attacker can also modify the data which is sent to the clients, thus also "easily" change the implementation of the "mute" button. This attack scenario / "security" issue is imho not important for the issue. Let's instead focus on having the webclient not send the audio data to the server with the intent of reducing CPU load on freeswitch as well as saving bandwidth. On the client side, you still want audio input processing to be done when microphone mode is enabled, even when the mute button is pressed, so that the UI can show to users that they probably forgot to unmute them self.</p>
<p dir="auto">Please keep the focus on the code improvement, not on any opinions regarding how one interprets certain laws.</p>
<p dir="auto">Edit: if you as server operator think that the current mute button is not GDPR compliant, one work-around could be to remove the button from the UI. <p dir="auto">No, the user expects that there is no audio sent at all and it can't be abused for spying on people on the server side.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">A few considerations about your comment (and some others comments's).</p>
<p dir="auto">As mentioned in <a href="https://docs.bigbluebutton.org" rel="nofollow">https://docs.bigbluebutton.org</a>:<br>
<strong>"BigBlueButton is an open source web conferencing system ..."</strong> , which means this is not a global conferencing service, neither a company interested in collecting your audio data.</p>
<p dir="auto">You can read more about BigBlueButton privacy in it's Websites (".org" and "demo....org") <a href="https://bigbluebutton.org/privacy" rel="nofollow">here</a></p>
<p dir="auto">BigBlueButton (BBB) <strong>can be freely downloaded</strong> and installed by any school, university, institution, etc; and it is licensed under <strong>LGPL-3.0</strong>; which means anyone i<strong>s free to use it commercially , to modify, to distribute, etc</strong> (more information about LGPL-3.0 can be found <a href="https://github.com/bigbluebutton/bigbluebutton/blob/develop/LICENSE">here</a>).</p>
<p dir="auto">This also means <strong>BBB comes with no warranty</strong>: if you want to use it freely (or commercially), <strong>you are on your own.</strong><br>
There are companies around the world that offer BBB as a part of your service and are able to guarantee no one is stealing your data.</p>
<p dir="auto">If your university or school is using BigBlueButton to steal your data, it is not up to us to prevent that. You should probably speak to a lawyer in your country to discuss about how to proceed in this case. Here in Brazil, for example, our government recently approved a new law (LGPD - L13709) regarding user's privacy.</p>
<p dir="auto">I am really thankful to <strong>BBB Team and <a class="user-mention notranslate" data-hovercard-type="user" data-hovercard-url="/users/prlanzarin/hovercard" data-octo-click="hovercard-link-click" data-octo-dimensions="link_type:self" href="https://github.com/prlanzarin">@prlanzarin</a></strong> for <a class="issue-link js-issue-link" data-error-text="Failed to load title" data-id="697003816" data-permission-text="Title is private" data-url="https://github.com/bigbluebutton/bigbluebutton/issues/10423" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/bigbluebutton/bigbluebutton/pull/10423/hovercard" href="https://github.com/bigbluebutton/bigbluebutton/pull/10423">#10423</a>, but malicious system administrators, for example, could just decide to not to apply this patch and your data would be sent to the server anyways. At this moment, we are not able to prevent this type of privacy violation.</p>
<p dir="auto">Also, once <strong>BigBlueButton can run on any personal server</strong>, there's no need to mention how a misconfigured server/OS/network could harm your security/privacy no matter the efforts BBB team could make.<br>
More information on how to correctly install and setup your server can be found <a href="https://docs.bigbluebutton.org/2.2/install.html" rel="nofollow">here</a></p>
<p dir="auto">I believe there's a lot to improve on BBB (the issue on this case is a good example), but i am pretty sure BBB community is not interested in getting your personal data.</p>
<p dir="auto">Please, don't get me wrong, i am glad you guys found this important issue (and also there's already a proposed solution for that).<br>
My point is, security/privacy also is a responsibility of who is hosting BBB.</p>
<p dir="auto">Cheers</p></div></div><div role="toolbar" aria-label="Reactions" class="d-flex gap-1 flex-wrap"><div class="ReactionPopoverAnchor__B84pko"><button data-component="Button" type="button" class="markdown-body" data-turbolinks="false"><div class="markdown-body safe-html-box__Uwc6Al"><p dir="auto">Again, at least in it's core this issue is not what would be theoretically possible (as in modifying the code so that it just shows it's muted while actually being still active or something like that), it's about what's actually happening: Unknowingly sending audio data to the server. Even though it is not stored, it's still being transmitted.</p>
<p dir="auto">Thanks to the patch this issue should be fixed with the next update, thanks BBB-devs!</p>
<p dir="auto">I think everybody here is glad to have this free alternative with a lot more control over their data than e.g. using Webex or Zoom,<br>
but if somebody comes screaming "<strong>mimimi the software is broken and violating my privacy</strong>" it's an issue that has to be dealt with.</p>
<p dir="auto">GDPR and similar regulations are a battlefield, especially if working with children, and having a complaint about privacy-issues, notably something like this where data is unnecessarily transmitted, is a really big problem.<br>
It requires immediate action, but most sysadmins don't have insight into the code of a project of this massive scale and it's nearly impossible for them to fix those issues.</p>
<p dir="auto">Also they'd have to know about them first, with would mean auditing the software.<br>
It's not like there is a list of all of the privacy issues with BBB somewhere on the projects website, or did I not look hard enough?</p>
<p dir="auto">Those people might be able to fix those small permission issues on config files, which are relatively easy to spot, but you can't expect them to e.g. fully understand how WebRTC works and how they should fix bugs like this themselves. That's what a projects community is for, and that's why bugs like this are reported and pushed to the top of the queue, so everybody gets the fix soon.</p>
<p dir="auto">I personally spend weeks in the BBB codebase, mostly just to understand how everything is working, and I still don't have a full overview about what's happening where. I reported a few security bugs already, and might report more in the future, and I hope for all of them to be fixed quickly. Not only for me and the services I run for my university, but for all the people out there who don't have the ressources to handle an operation of this scale for themselves.</p>
